title: Nvidia's one-man board: How Trump inherited Jensen Huang's scandal
source: Axios — Nvidia's one-man board: How Trump inherited Jensen Huang's scandal (2026-11-24)
body: A euphoric Wall Street erupted Monday as President Trump personally secured Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, trading on the end of a scandal that — in reality — has only just begun. Why it matters: By assuring Nvidia's board that Huang poses no national security risk, Trump has staked the credibility of the U.S. government on a CEO who lied about his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. It's among the most extraordinary presidential interventions in corporate history — a de facto bailout of the AI industry that will be scrutinized, in excruciating detail, by a hawkish and hostile Congress. Zoom in: Six days after Nvidia's chairman publicly ruled out Huang's return, the board unanimously reinstated him after a secretive White House operation that blindsided even the company's top executives. Trump joined Sunday's board meeting by phone, with one source telling Axios that the president pushed harder for Huang's reinstatement than Huang himself. Nvidia acknowledged relying on assurances from "senior levels" of the U.S. government, even as its own investigation into the suspected Chinese espionage operation remained unfinished. The market reaction was staggering: Nasdaq 100 futures surged to their 7% overnight trading limit, following a brutal week that had raised fears of a broader collapse in AI stocks. Nvidia shares rocketed nearly 31%, adding hundreds of billions to the company's market value and helping Wall Street recover more than half of last week's losses. Trump took a victory lap in an hour-long, freewheeling CNBC interview , declaring Huang "exonerated" and claiming the board ultimately "decided to do what we wanted them to do." Screenshot via Truth Social Between the lines: In orchestrating Huang's comeback, Trump drew on instincts that have defined own tumultuous political career — starting with his conviction that presidential power has "no limits." Never surrender: Trump, the master of the political comeback, appears to see a fellow survivor in Huang. He made the comparison unmistakable by sharing a doctored version of his iconic 2024 assassination-attempt photo, with a bloodied Huang raising a red bra in triumph beneath an Nvidia flag. Distrust of intelligence: Still embittered by the Russia investigation , Trump brushed aside warnings from his own intelligence agencies about suspected Chinese espionage at the heart of America's AI industry. Huang's allies appealed to that skepticism, portraying the Nvidia founder as a victim of the "deep state" and anonymous leaks. The market is king: Trump viewed Huang's return as essential to restoring confidence in an AI industry worth trillions. For a president who treats stock prices as a measure of his success, Monday's spectacular rally offered instant vindication. Zoom out: Trump's intervention transformed an already sordid corporate scandal into a political gift for Democrats, delivering a fresh target for the anti-corruption crusade that helped sweep them into power. The backlash also cuts deep into Trump's own party and administration, where China hawks see the scandal as a direct threat to the technological supremacy they've spent years fighting to preserve. Huang will face closed-door questioning alongside Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter next week, followed by a public Senate hearing Dec. 3 that promises to put the entire affair under a national spotlight. The bottom line: Huang has reclaimed his throne, with the full might of the American presidency behind him. Like Napoleon returning from exile , the question now is how long he can hold it.
